project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Demonstrate vessel-wide battery systems that extend electric range and battery life while allowing higher propulsion power and rapid recharging.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Demonstrate all-battery vessel operation in representative service. Cover vessel energy management, battery durability, vessel–port interfaces and approaches to fast or offshore charging.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Ship operators need more range and higher power without making batteries wear out faster. Short port calls make fast and reliable charging especially important.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Demonstrate at least 150 nautical miles of battery-only range, equivalent to 277.8 kilometres for inland navigation, plus more than 5 megawatts of peak propulsion power. Give safety recommendations from testing.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Show which shipping profiles can operate entirely on batteries and which conditions improve battery life, range and reliable charging. Make the results applicable to more than one vessel type.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Expected Outcome
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Set out business cases and a deployment and replication roadmap. Report evidence to the Zero Emission Waterborne Transport partnership (the European research and industry initiative for cleaner shipping).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners in three different eligible countries. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: The project should build strong collaboration among industry, training providers and higher education. The call encourages shipyards, equipment manufacturers and suppliers from the European Union and European Economic Area.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: Connect ship, port and charging work across the supply chain. Plan industry and training cooperation, and show European added value in use and ownership of results.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on maritime battery electrification and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can analyse corresponding grid capacity as part of a substantive port or offshore charging design. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could take part in maritime battery electrification without receiving a grant. As an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant), it could analyse corresponding grid capacity as part of a substantive port or offshore charging design. It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could analyse corresponding grid capacity as part of a substantive port or offshore charging design. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could assess the connection capacity and demand peaks of an aggregated port or offshore charging use case. Tie that contribution to the vessel–port interface tested by the project.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: Improve systems beyond simply scaling up commercial batteries. Innovate in battery operation, vessel energy management and charging as well as electrical design.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Innovation covers vessel-wide energy control, charging, thermal and battery management, modular retrofits and interfaces with ports.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Develop and test onboard systems and validate performance at full scale. Develop rapid in-route charging concepts and assess which service profiles can use them.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 8 (technology readiness level: a complete, qualified system) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Demonstrate on a full-scale vessel in representative service. Short-sea, ferry or offshore cases cover vessels from 400 to 6,500 gross tonnage (a measure of enclosed size). Inland cases cover vessels 86–135 metres long on free-flowing upstream routes.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Coordinate propulsion, onboard loads, battery management and charging in one design. Address the vessel interface with port operations and available electrical capacity.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Show at least 150 nautical miles of battery-only range and more than 5 megawatts of peak propulsion power. Validate higher charging-cycle capability and assess credible service profiles and economics.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: The project should build strong collaboration between industry, training providers and higher education institutions. Define operating needs with ship and port actors.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: Use field testing to inform safety guidance for the new battery installation and ship systems. Address relevant marine battery guidance, battery-room fire safety and the effect on operating plans.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Specific conditions

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 20 million for maritime battery electrification. It expects 2 awards.
- Grant request: around EUR 10 million per project is indicative. The Commission can select a different request.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · p. 42 · Overview of this call
Enhanced electric operation and battery durability (ZEWT Partnership) · Budget overview

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards maritime battery electrification.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for maritime battery electrification using the cost categories allowed by the grant. The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) specifies how those costs can be claimed.
- Eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow): Personnel, purchases and eligible subcontracting.
- Overheads and value added tax (tax on purchases): The indirect-cost rate (overheads such as general office expenses) is 25% of the eligible direct-cost base after exclusions. value added tax is eligible where it is unrecoverable and the cost otherwise qualifies.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 32 · Budget categories and cost eligibility rules
EU Annotated Grant Agreement · p. 143 · Value added tax
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for maritime battery electrification around the initial advance and later payments.
- Payment model: Usually pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant), then interim payments linked to reporting and a final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: 5–8% of the maximum grant is deducted from pre-financing for the mutual insurance mechanism (a common fund covering grant recovery risks).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 257–260 · Specific conditions

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for maritime battery electrification through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 14 April 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal). Part B is limited to 40 pages.
- Opening: 15 December 2026.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for maritime battery electrification.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting maritime battery electrification is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around five months after the deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): The indicative signature date is around eight months after the deadline.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the portal’s forms to submit the proposal and supporting documents for maritime battery electrification.
- Application form: Complete Part A online and upload Part B as a fixed-format document with the required annexes.
- Registration: Enter a participant identification code for each beneficiary (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entity (organisations legally linked to funded partners).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Maritime battery electrification proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation.
- Thresholds: At least 3/5 per criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Weighting: Impact is multiplied by 1.5 for the ranking.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Demonstrating new marine battery systems brings additional conditions on European value creation and use of results.
- Conditional — Satellite services: If the project uses satellite-based Earth observation, positioning, navigation or timing, it must use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing. Other services may supplement them.
- Exception — Ownership and control: Entities directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established in China cannot participate.
- Exception — Transfer of results: The granting authority may object to a transfer of ownership or to exclusive licensing (giving another party sole rights to use the results) for up to four years after the project ends.
